```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

TRSC measures temporal movement in prediction geometry rather than Euclidean
distance between raw donor-share vectors. The empirical geometry is the
uncentered donor-state second moment and is allowed to be singular.

```{r geometry}
library(TRSC)

reference_states <- cbind(
  A = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5),
  B = c(2, 0, 1, 3, 2),
  A_duplicate = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
)

geometry <- trsc_geometry(reference_states)
geometry
```

Because `A` and `A_duplicate` are identical in the reference states, the
empirical second-moment matrix is rank deficient. This is a legitimate state of
the model, not an error.

## Equivalent raw representations

```{r equivalent}
w <- c(A = 1, B = 0, A_duplicate = 0)
v <- c(A = 0, B = 0, A_duplicate = 1)

trsc_profile_distance(geometry, w, v)
trsc_profile_equivalent(geometry, w, v)

trsc_profile_coordinates(geometry, w)
trsc_profile_coordinates(geometry, v)
```

The two raw vectors differ completely as donor shares but have zero predictive
distance at the supplied empirical geometry.

## Interpretation boundary

The factor stored in `geometry$B` provides computational coordinates for the
supplied empirical geometry. If that geometry was learned from a finite
calibration sample, its extra empirical null directions are not automatically
population-null directions. Empirical rank and null dimension are therefore
diagnostics, not population-identification certificates.
